headline_marked: 760m cubic feet: [[LNG supply increases]] as Summit and Accelerate terminals resume
headline: 760m cubic feet: LNG supply increases as Summit and Accelerate terminals resume
summary: Gas supply to the national grid has risen following the partial and full resumption of two major LNG terminals, providing relief from recent shortages.
details: The national grid is currently receiving approximately 760 million cubic feet of gas from the Summit and Accelerate Energy terminals. This marks an increase in supply starting from the early hours of Saturday, August 15.

The Summit LNG terminal has returned to full operation after a new LNG carrier arrived, overcoming previous weather-related delays. It is currently supplying 460 million cubic feet daily, with expectations to reach 500 million cubic feet soon.

Previously, a carrier destined for the Summit terminal was forced to return to Singapore on August 10 due to severe weather and high winds, which had reduced the terminal's daily supply by about 300 million cubic feet.

The Accelerate Energy LNG terminal, which had been shut down due to technical faults, has partially resumed operations. It is now supplying an average of 300 million cubic feet daily to the national grid.
Repairs at the Accelerate terminal are ongoing and are expected to be completed by August 19. Once finished, its daily supply is projected to increase to 600 million cubic feet.
Authorities state that once both terminals are fully operational by August 19, the total LNG supply to the national grid will return to its normal average of 1,100 million cubic feet per day.

The Accelerate Energy LNG terminal, which had been shut down due to technical faults, has partially resumed operations. It is now supplying an average of 300 million cubic feet daily to the national grid.

Repairs at the Accelerate terminal are ongoing and are expected to be completed by August 19. Once finished, its daily supply is projected to increase to 600 million cubic feet.

Authorities state that once both terminals are fully operational by August 19, the total LNG supply to the national grid will return to its normal average of 1,100 million cubic feet per day.

headline_marked: Tight security at Dhanmondi 32 as [[two men are detained]] for paying respects
headline: Tight security at Dhanmondi 32 as two men are detained for paying respects
summary: Police have stepped up security at the ruins of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's residence ahead of his death anniversary, detaining several individuals attempting to place flowers.
details: Police have intensified security around Dhanmondi 32, the former residence of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, ahead of the anniversary of his assassination.
Several individuals were detained by law enforcement after attempting to place flowers at the site to pay their respects.
Reports indicate that some individuals were detained after shouting 'Joy Bangla' slogans and allegedly distributing singaras and recording videos at the location.
Police remain on high alert to maintain order and prevent any unauthorized gatherings at the ruins of the residence.
The increased security presence includes barriers and a significant number of personnel deployed to restrict access to the area.
